security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU hardcodes Smnip CSR addresses using the pre-fix (incorrect) values from the draft spec: msp at 0x348 instead of 0x349, ssp at 0x148 instead of 0x149, mithreshold at 0xFB1 instead of 0x347, mipreemptcfg at 0x347 instead of 0x348, or sithreshold at 0x1B1 instead of 0x147. Any CSR read/write using stale address constants will access the wrong logical register, causing msp writes to alias into mipreemptcfg (0x348 collision) and mithreshold to land at an unmapped custom-range address (0xFB1) that may read as zero or be silently ignored.
security_spec.summary: Smnip CSR address renumbering: 5 CSRs had their addresses fixed—stale QEMU code using old addresses will access wrong registers (msp/mipreemptcfg collide at 0x348, mithreshold at invalid 0xFB1), causing silent corruption of interrupt preemption state and stack pointer values

findings.finding: Smnip CSRs (mpistatus 0x346, mithreshold 0x347, mipreemptcfg 0x348, spistatus 0x146, sithreshold 0x147) are not yet defined in the codebase. No stale/wrong address constants exist — the extension is simply unimplemented. There is no aliasing or collision risk because none of these addresses are claimed by other CSR definitions in cpu_bits.h. The spec (riscv-fast-interrupt/src/aclic.adoc:679-681) confirms correct addresses are 0x346 (mpistatus), 0x347 (mithreshold), 0x348 (mipreemptcfg).
findings.snippet: (Smnip extension not yet implemented — no CSR definitions found)

findings.finding: The scountinhibit_pred function now correctly checks MENVCFG_CDE before allowing access to scountinhibit, matching the spec requirement that counter delegation must be enabled. No security issue.
Added validation that rejects MSI translation when IO translation mode is BARE (disabled), preventing misconfiguration. Not a security concern — this is a correctness improvement.
